title: Gifts From the Sage
captions: The next morning, Vishvamitra smiled at Rama. “I am very pleased with you, my child. Today I will give you a great gift.”
Facing the rising sun in the east, the sage chanted sacred mantras. He gave Rama the divine astras, the shining weapons of the gods.
One by one, the astras appeared before Rama in glowing forms. With folded hands they said, “We are here to serve you, Rama.”
Rama touched them gently and said, “Stay in my mind, and come to me whenever I call you.”
Then Rama asked for one more thing. “Please teach me how to call the astras back, too.” Pleased, the sage taught him that as well.
Rama's heart was full of thanks. He bowed before his great teacher with folded hands.
As they walked on, Rama saw a peaceful grove at the foot of a hill. “Great sage, whose hermitage is that?” he asked.
lesson: Vishvamitra gave Rama the most precious gifts he had: knowledge and the divine astras. Rama did not grow proud. He bowed to his teacher with a thankful heart, and he even asked to learn how to call the astras back, so that such power would be used with care. In our tradition, the guru is honoured like a parent, and Kritajnata means remembering and thanking those who help us grow.
card_lesson: Rama received wonderful gifts, but he did not grow proud. He bowed to his teacher with a thankful heart. Kritajnata means remembering and thanking those who help us grow.
question: Who is a teacher who has helped you learn something special? How could you thank them?
